goal: Adds a bitcoin-mine test program that connects to a running bitcoin-node over IPC and exercises the Mining interface end to end.
Gives developers and reviewers a concrete C++ libmultiprocess client and functional test that other IPC/mining work can build on.
reviewability: Ready to review now, no rebase or CI issues, and the author has kept it current through many rebases over two years.
One architecture question (whether the binary should build by default and ship in releases) is unresolved but the author agrees and it does not block reviewing the existing code.
agreement: Broad support with several Concept/Tested ACKs from ismaelsadeeq, Sjors, and BrandonOdiwuor after hands-on testing.

Standing, acknowledged caveat: sedited and fanquake think the binary should not be built by default or shipped in releases, and the author agreed a separate CMake option is needed but has not yet implemented it (sedited, fanquake).
Ongoing but nonblocking naming/scope debate about whether this should be renamed or moved to an examples/tests directory (Sjors, sedited, ismaelsadeeq).

result.summary: This PR adds a new `bitcoin-mine` executable that connects to a running `bitcoin-node` process over IPC (unix socket) and calls `interfaces::Mining` methods, including creating a block template and submitting a mined solution. It adds a matching functional test (`feature_mine.py`), CMake build wiring, a `bitcoin mine` subcommand on the `bitcoin` wrapper, and moves `interface_ui` into the common library so the new binary can use `InitError`/`InitWarning`. It has been under continuous rebase and refinement for over two years as related IPC/mining interface PRs landed.
result.problem: There is currently no standalone C++ (libmultiprocess-based) IPC client in the tree to exercise cross-process serialization and connection handling for the Mining interface, and no example for developers building similar IPC clients (e.g. Stratum v2 template providers). This leaves a coverage gap that Python-based functional IPC tests cannot fill because they do not exercise the libmultiprocess client stack.

open_concerns: Whether the binary should be gated behind its own CMake option so it is not built/shipped as part of ordinary or release builds (sedited, fanquake); author agreed but has not yet implemented the separate variable.

Whether the executable and its scope should be renamed/reframed (e.g. `test_bitcoin-mining`, or moved to an examples/tests directory) to make clear it is a demo/test artifact rather than a real mining tool (sedited, ismaelsadeeq, Sjors); no final decision reached.

Minor robustness edge cases in the mining loop (handling tip changes mid-mining, bounding max tries) raised by ismaelsadeeq and w0xlt; some addressed (nullptr check, negative -maxtries), others left as documented limitations by design choice.
resolved_concerns: Early design to have bitcoin-mine auto-spawn bitcoin-node was dropped for simplicity per Sjors' suggestion, deferred to a follow-up branch.
Socket path length bug on macOS caught by Sjors and fixed by the author.
-debug=ipc logging not working, fixed by author after Sjors' testing.
Windows resource file added after maflcko's nit.
fanquake's NACK on adding the binary to the Guix/Maintenance target list was resolved by dropping that change.

uncertainties: Whether the outstanding CMake-option/shipping concern from sedited and fanquake has been addressed in commits after the shown diff, since the timeline extends past the provided patch.
Whether the naming/scope debate (test_bitcoin-mining vs bitcoin-mine, examples folder) will materially change the final shape of the PR, which would affect reviewability going forward.
How much weight to give the author's own admission that the original stratum-v2 motivation is 'a bit stale' when scoring mining-category importance.
result.card: Adds `bitcoin-mine`, a standalone libmultiprocess-based C++ test/example program that connects to `bitcoin-node` over IPC and exercises `interfaces::Mining` (getTip, createNewBlock, submitSolution), plus a matching functional test and CMake/build wiring. It fills a real coverage gap since existing functional IPC tests are Python-based and don't exercise the libmultiprocess client stack (Sjors), and code from it has already been reused in #32297 and #33201. Review has been sustained over two years with several Concept/Tested ACKs (Sjors, ismaelsadeeq, BrandonOdiwuor), but there is a live, author-acknowledged but unimplemented concern from sedited and fanquake that the binary should be gated behind its own build option rather than shipping by default. No hard blocking dependency; the PR is otherwise mergeable and reviewable now.
